name: Prevest Denpro Ltd
title: Prevest Denpro Ltd - 543363 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Dental materials maker grew revenue 13.9% to INR71.81 cr with 38.6% EBITDA margin, but traditional capacity sits at only 67-68% utilisation and no capex or capacity-addition guidance was given.

utilisation.quote: the company is working at a capacity utilization of, say, around 67% to 68% of its total installed capacity

summary.headline: Prevest DenPro FY26 revenue rose 13.9% to INR71.81 crore and PAT rose 12.9% to INR20.49 crore, with PAT margin at 26.7%.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 13.9% to INR71.81 crore, with exports up 17.58% and domestic up 9%. EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR29.62 crore, though the EBITDA margin of 38.6% moderated slightly year on year. Q4 FY26 revenue grew only 2.63% to INR18.94 crore due to geopolitical disruption and shipping issues, but Q4 profitability outpaced sales, with EBITDA margin at 40.87% and PAT up 13.23% to INR5.82 crore. Management launched disinfectant commercialisation and set up a UAE subsidiary, whose operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 domestic sales grew 9%; H2 domestic sales rose 12.72% YoY and 16.19% HoH. Management cited floods and GST changes as H1 drags.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export sales grew 17.58%; H2 exports rose 11.66% YoY and 3.56% HoH. The company says it covers about 90-92 countries.

segments.name: US (Axiodent and private label)
segments.commentary: US business grew about 37.58% (also cited as 38%) in FY26, driven by online sales, direct orders and private-label business won at US exhibitions.

segments.name: Oradox oral care
segments.commentary: Sales declined about 2% in FY26 because US MoCRA-related exports and a planned Dubai consignment did not ship. Management expects 2-3 new launches and a recovery.

segments.name: 3D printing (resins and printers)
segments.commentary: 3D resin revenue rose about 40.5% YoY. 3D printers (brand Omni, sales started November 2025) rose about 162% from a low base.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Oradox to compensate for the FY26 shortfall this year, supported by 2-3 new product launches.
UAE subsidiary expected to start online sales in Dubai the following month, after product registration; commercial operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.
Company aims for a fully indigenous 3D printer by 2028.
Management expects at least 40% of dental-office procedures to have a digital workflow within five years.
Management is cautious on global uncertainty but sees the domestic market, Tier 2/3 expansion and disinfectants as growth drivers.
capex_capacity: Traditional capacity utilisation is about 67-68% of installed capacity; at full installed capacity, turnover would be about INR125 crore (Vinay Jamwal).
New production lines (digital dentistry, resins, disinfectants, oral health) are running at about 18-20% utilisation and are expected to rise.
Four R&D test licences for new agents (caries removal, endodontic irrigants, self-etching resins, periodontal gels) are at TRL 7, with two products launched in the market in the month of the call.
Import substitution of raw materials is in progress through in-house development.
Subsidiaries in the UAE (opened February 2026) and the US (Axiodent) are operating; two sales staff employed in Dubai.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian manufacturing cost advantage and high import duties make it hard for MNCs to beat the company on price; it also cites quality certifications.
The company is an OEM supplier to about 3-4 large companies and expects to add a couple more in the next two years.
Competitors named for digital dentistry include Ivoclar, Dentsply and 3Shape; management says digital dentistry is a level playing field, unlike legacy products where MNCs have first-mover advantage.
Disinfectants launched this year, with an early customer response described as highly encouraging; no revenue figure given.
Oradox was hit by US MoCRA cosmetic-regulation requirements and by the Middle East conflict, which blocked a planned Dubai consignment.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth slowed over the last 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 export growth of 17.5% is satisfactory given geopolitical headwinds, and that the company is shifting share from disrupted Asian markets to other geographies across 90-92 countries.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is spent on R&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sai Kalyan did not give a figure and said it would be provided later. He described two products launched, four licences at TRL 7 and import substitution work.

qa_highlights.question: What do the UAE and US subsidiaries do, and how is Dubai responding?
qa_highlights.answer: The US subsidiary, Axiodent, drove US growth of about 37.58% through online sales, direct orders and private labelling. The Dubai subsidiary opened in February 2026, hired two sales staff and is registering products for online sales expected next month.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Jamwal said traditional capacity runs at 67-68% utilisation, which would imply about INR125 crore turnover at full installed capacity. New lines run at 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove domestic performance and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaibhav Munjal cited expansion of Tier 2/3 distribution, a larger in-house sales team and new products such as disinfectants and Rotoflex. H1 was hit by floods and GST changes, and H2 recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How is Oradox trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said sales fell about 2% because US and Dubai exports were blocked by MoCRA rules and the war. Management expects recovery through marketing, direct-to-doctor programmes and 2-3 launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3D printing opportunity and right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said digital dentistry is a level field where the company has a slight edge, with 3D resin revenue up about 40.5% and printer sales up about 162%, and an indigenous printer targeted for 2028.

risks_watch: Q4 revenue growth of only 2.63% was hit by war-related shipping disruption and customer order delays; the trend in Q1 FY27 needs monitoring.
Capacity utilisation is 67-68% for traditional lines and only 18-20% for new lines, so new-line ramp-up is unproven.
Dubai subsidiary has not yet started commercial operations and depends on the Middle East situation.
Oradox is declining and needs the planned launches and US/Dubai registrations to recover.
The R&D spend figure was not provided and the disinfectant revenue contribution is undisclosed.
Management said the Chairman was ill, and the June 2 call was cancelled; continuity of leadership needs watching.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, especially the US and export recovery, but cautious on global uncertainty. Management was evasive on specifics such as R&D spend, disinfectant revenue and the Oradox revenue base, and deferred several questions to later follow-up.
key_quotes: Financial year 2025-'26 was a year of steady growth, disciplined execution and continued strategic progress.
Despite these external challenges, our business continued to demonstrate resilience.
Our focus on operational efficiency resulted in further improvement in margins during the quarter.

financial_highlights.value: EBITDA INR8.32 crore, margin 40.87%; PAT INR5.82 crore, margin 28.61%

adds.what: New production lines (digital dentistry, resins, disinfectants, oral health) already running at about 18-20% utilisation; not a new addition

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management expects Oradox to recover via 2-3 launches, the UAE subsidiary to start Dubai online sales, and domestic/Tier 2-3 and disinfectants to drive growth, but these are largely unquantified and Q4 revenue grew only 2.63%.
